To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed improved detectors for the case of imperfect MIMO channel estimation and have shown, via numerical results, that the improved detectors can achieve significant performance improvement compared with classical mismatched receivers.
the use of the proposed improved detectors can lead to a significant reduction of the bit-error rate in a MIMO system with imperfect channel estimation.

we have developed improved iterative detectors for MIMO systems with imperfect channel estimates and that we have demonstrated the effectiveness of these detectors by means of numerical results for Rayleigh fading channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of iterative MIMO signal detection schemes that are able to account for imperfect channel estimation.
the design of efficient iterative detectors that can be used in practical MIMO systems, which have to deal with imperfect channel estimation.
the design of iterative MIMO signal detectors that take into account the channel estimation errors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed improved detectors can be applied to a wide range of practical scenarios and can be implemented in a simple way.

the proposed improved detectors can provide a significant performance improvement compared with the classially used detectors, especially under fast fading, without a considerable increase of receiver complexity.

the improved iterative MIMO detectors are more robust to channel-estimation error than the classically used iterative MIMO detectors and the mismatched detectors, especially in the case where the number of pilots used for channel estimation is relatively small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the improved iterative detectors are capable of mitigating the effect of channel-estimation error, and thus, they can provide an efficient trade-off between performance and complexity.
, in the context of iterative receivers, the proposed improved detector is a good alternative for MIMO systems with imperfect channel estimation.

the proposed iterative detectors are able to exploit the channel-estimator errors to improve the system performance, and thus, they can be considered as a generalization of the classically used iterative detectors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a MIMO system using iterative detection, the channel-estimator output should be taken into account to improve the performance.
it is beneficial to account for channel-estimation error in MIMO detectors, even when the channel-estimator performance is not very good.
, by taking channel-estimation error into account, the proposed iterative detectors outperform the classically used detectors, especially in the case of few pilots.
